The Caribbean - bottom line: Gang violence takes toll on Tavares Gardens Primary.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: Gang violence takes toll on Tavares Gardens Primary.
The impact of gang violence in Payne Land, St Andrew is being felt in the classrooms of Tavares Gardens Primary School, where only 80 students are enrolled at an institution built to accommodate 415. Principal Terriann Nisbeth said repeated clashes between warring factions have left some parents afraid to send their children to school and, in some cases, unable to collect them after dismissal.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: AI could decide whether and how travellers vacation in Jamaica.
WESTERN BUREAU: Jamaica is moving to make its tourism industry ready for a future in which artificial intelligence could help determine not only whether a traveller visits the island, but where that visitor stays, eats, explores, and spends. The Jamaica Tourist Board (JTB) has begun examining the country’s tourism information infrastructure as AI-powered assistants increasingly move beyond answering travellers’ questions towards recommending destinations, building itineraries, and, eventually, completing bookings.

Drones are used to achieve air superiority, a reconnaissance advantage, and highly precise strategic strikes along the front lines. South Asia - bottom line: 'Heinous and cowardly': UNSC condemns Kohat terrorist attack, calls for accountability for perpetrators, sponsors.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: 'Heinous and cowardly': UNSC condemns Kohat terrorist attack, calls for accountability for perpetrators, sponsors.
The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) on Wednesday condemned last week’s terrorist attack in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kohat district, calling for the perpetrators and sponsors of the attack to be held accountable. At least 23 people were killed in the September 18’s deadly two-pronged assault, including 17 policemen and six civilians. After detonating an explosives-laden vehicle near a mosque in old Police Lines during Friday prayers, terrorists stormed the compound and attacked police facilities. KP police said eight terrorists were killed in retaliatory action by police and security forces.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: Saudi king denounces Houthis in rare rebuke.
• Rebels accuse Riyadh of deadly strikes as thousands flee • 154 people reportedly killed in fighting over past two days • G7 calls on Yemeni group to halt military actions, attacks on shipping • UK commits air-to-air refuelling support for Saudis SANAA: The king of Saudi Arabia denounced Yemen’s Houthis as a “terrorist militia” in a rare statement on Tue­sday reacting to an attack that authorities said targeted the holy city of Makkah last week.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: 8 drones launched by Afghan Taliban shot down near Torkham border, Kohat: security sources.
The armed forces on Wednesday shot down eight drones launched by the Afghan Taliban after they entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat, according to security sources. The sources said the drones were intercepted by the air defence systems, which they described as “active and vigilant”. “The armed forces and the ‘Shaheens’ of the Pakistan Air Force professionally thwarted the Afghan Taliban regime’s cowardly attempt to target public areas,” security sources said.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: With reconstruction stalled, Gazans shelter in buildings at risk of collapse.
In her Gaza City apartment, Heba Arafat walks uphill across a living room slanted at a steep angle after Israeli airstrikes caused the building’s foundations to collapse, leaving the entire structure tilted. Like thousands of people in Gaza, Arafat chose to risk living in an apartment building damaged during nearly three years of Israel’s military actions, with countless Israeli airstrikes on the Palestinian territory. “We were forced to live here because we had nowhere else to go. All of our homes were destroyed, our land was razed and we have nothing left,” said Arafat, 47.
